    AI Overview
    El Salvador, a Central American nation, is a sovereign republic with a population of over 6 million, a history marked by conflict and growth, and a culture heavily influenced by Catholicism. It is officially Spanish-speaking, with the U.S. dollar and Bitcoin as its legal tender. The capital is San Salvador. 
    Key Details About El Salvador 
    • Location: Central America, bordered by Honduras, Guatemala, and the Pacific Ocean.
    • History: Declared independence from Spain in 1821, was part of the Federal Republic of Central America, and later a sovereign state. It experienced a 12-year civil war (1979–1992)
      .
    • Government: A multiparty constitutional republic, currently led by President Nayib Bukele.
    • Economy: Uses the U.S. dollar and Bitcoin as legal tender.
    • Culture: Primarily Roman Catholic. 
    Other "Salvador" Meanings 
    • Salvador, Brazil: A major coastal city, capital of the state of Bahia, known for its colonial architecture and Afro-Brazilian culture.
    • Film/TV: "Salvador" (1986), a film by Oliver Stone, and a 2026 Netflix series. 
    Major Cities in El Salvador 
    • San Salvador: Capital and largest city.
    • Suchitoto: Known for its colonial charm.
    • Santa Ana: Known for the Santa Ana Volcano. 
    Major Tourist Attractions in El Salvador 
    • Santa Ana Volcano: An active volcano with a turquoise crater lake.
    • Coatepeque Caldera: A large, scenic volcanic lake.
    • Ruta de las Flores: A scenic route through mountain towns, coffee plantations, and flower-filled landscapes.
    • Beaches: Known for surf spots like El Tunco. 
    Key Historical Events in El Salvador 
    • 1821: Independence from Spain.
    • 1841: Became a sovereign state.
    • 1979–1992: Civil War.
    • 1992: Chapultepec Peace Accords.
    • 2021: Adoption of Bitcoin as legal tender. 
    Culture and Religion in El Salvador 
    • Religion: Catholicism is the dominant religion, with a significant presence of evangelical Protestantism.
    • Culture: A mix of indigenous (Pipil) and Spanish influences, evident in food, music, and art.
    • Language: Spanish is the official language. 
    Economy and Currency of El Salvador 
    • Currency: United States dollar (since 2001) and Bitcoin (since 2021).
    • Industry: Agriculture (coffee, sugar), manufacturing, and services.
    • Key Sectors: Tourism and technology are growing industries.

    AI Overview
    El Salvador's history is defined by indigenous Pipil civilization, Spanish conquest, and a long struggle with authoritarian military rule and massive social inequality. Following independence from Spain in 1821 and the Coffee boom, extreme wealth disparity led to a brutal 12-year civil war (1980–1992). A 1992 peace accord transformed rebels into politicians, but the country later struggled with gang violence before adopting stricter security measures in recent years. 
    Key Periods in El Salvador's History
    • Pre-Columbian Era & Spanish Conquest:
      Originally inhabited by the Pocomam, Chortí, Lenca, and ultimately the Pipil people. Spanish conquistador Pedro de Alvarado conquered the region in 1524, establishing colonial rule. 
    • Independence:
      El Salvador declared independence from Spain in 1821 as part of the Captaincy General of Guatemala, eventually becoming an independent republic in 1839 after the collapse of the Federal Republic of Central America. 
    • The Coffee Republic & Military Rule:
      In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, land ownership was concentrated in the hands of a few elites (the "14 families"). A 1932 farmers' revolt resulted in a brutal military crackdown, after which military leaders ruled almost exclusively until 1979. 
    • Civil War (1980–1992):
      The inequality and political repression led to a brutal civil war between the military government and the FMLN leftist rebels. The war resulted in over 70,000 deaths and high levels of displacement. 
    • Post-War Era:
      The 1992 Chapultepec Peace Accords ended the war, allowing the FMLN to become a legal political party. In 2001, El Salvador adopted the US dollar as its currency. 
    • Recent History:
      The country faced severe gang violence for years following the war. Since the late 2010s, a major crackdown led by President Nayib Bukele has drastically reduced crime rates but raised concerns over human rights, say the BBC News profile](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-19402222) and [other reports. 
    For more information on the civil war's impact, see the Frommers history article.

      Tourist Destinations. What are the popular tourist destinations in El Salvador?
      About this result
      Feedback
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Popular tourist destinations in El Salvador include world-renowned surf beaches like Playa El Tunco and El Sunzal, the hiking trails of Cerro Verde National Park (specifically the Santa Ana volcano), and the ancient Mayan ruins at Joya de Cerén. Visitors also enjoy scenic Lake Coatepeque, the cultural "Ruta de las Flores," and the capital city, San Salvador. 
      Here are the top attractions, categorized:
      • Surfing and Beaches:
        Playa El Tunco and El Sunzal in La Libertad are famous for their nightlife, surf schools, and cafes. Other popular spots include El Zonte, Mizata, and the tranquil beaches at El Cuco. 
      • Volcanoes and Nature:
        The Santa Ana Volcano (Ilamatepec) is a top hike with a turquoise crater lake at its summit. El Boquerón National Park features a stunning crater-within-a-crater, while the Conchagua Volcano offers panoramic coastal views. 
      • Archaeological Sites:
        Joya de Cerén, a UNESCO World Heritage site known as the "Pompeii of Central America," provides a glimpse into daily Mayan life. Tazumal and San Andrés are other significant ancient ruins. 
      • Culture and Towns:
        The Ruta de las Flores (Route of the Flowers) is a scenic route through colorful colonial towns known for coffee, murals, and markets. Suchitoto is a charming colonial town near the massive Lake Suchitlán. 
      • Key Sightseeing:
        Lake Coatepeque is a large, popular crater lake, while the Iglesia El Rosario in San Salvador is renowned for its unique, colorful architecture. 
      The country is compact, making it easy to combine beach, nature, and cultural trips into a short visit.

        El Salvador, officially the Republic of El Salvador, is a country in Central America. It is bordered on the northeast by Honduras, on the northwest by Guatemala, and on the south by the Pacific Ocean. El Salvador's capital and largest city is San Salvador.
